items.content:
RT @WindowsLatest: Microsoft has finally admitted why Windows 11 needs to use less RAM, and it comes down to something everyone buying a PC in 2026 already knows: memory is expensive again.

Pavan Davuluri, Microsoft’s Windows chief, said it clearly:

“I do think memory is top of mind for us right now in the industry, especially as we look at the rising cost of memory for computers across the board. For us, as a Windows team, we have clear efforts around driving better utilization of memory.”

Microsoft has now made “memory optimization for 8GB and above” an official Windows priority for the rest of 2026.

Davuluri says the work is happening across the memory manager, memory compression, and the frameworks that sit on top of Windows.

“We do definitely have work when it comes to compressing memory and making sure we’re more efficient on the platform,” he said.

Microsoft is trying to make Windows take memory only when a capability is actually being used.

“You only take the memory cost as and when you use the capability. Otherwise, the base system gets a little bit more efficient across the board.”

I’m glad Microsoft is reducing Windows 11's memory management, WinUI 3, WebView2, and Chromium efficiency, and hopefully, one day, Microsoft will also fix its own web-based apps...

items.content:
a developer cant comprehend the full system they’re building. as things get added, it grows beyond their comprehension and mental model. this complexity is fine as long as the system works. 

the same complexity also makes exploitation a scarce expertise. a few people can put in the effort to understand parts of it and find ways in.

when you introduce a new agent that is faster and better, things get weird. all that complexity starts becoming obvious, and the agent can find flaws and exploit them at a scale other agents couldnt

if you want security to be a property, dont build things you cant reason about. secure by design means reducing complexity, keeping the system comprehensible, and using formal methods to make sure there are no states you dont expect

it rationally makes sense to get as many trusted researchers and companies as possible red teaming your companies, your models, and the infrastructure they depend on.

RT @The_Cyber_News: ‼️ BREAKING - ShinyHunters Member Detained in Jordan, Reportedly Helping FBI Identify Fellow Hackers

Details: https://t.co/OV2TpHHWv0

A suspected ShinyHunters member has been detained in Jordan and is reportedly helping the FBI identify other hackers linked to the group. Reuters reported on October 3 that three people familiar with the matter confirmed the detention of Saif al-Din Khader, whose alleged online nickname is Rey. 

Two sources said Jordanian authorities took Khader into custody on Tuesday, September 29. They also said he was helping the FBI and law enforcement agencies worldwide locate other group members. Reuters could not establish why he was detained or where he was being held, and attempts to contact him and his family were unsuccessful.
